@Devon Tuma @Eric Wieser @Quang Dao, I was browsing the state of PRs and noticed cslib#803. Just wanted to flag that in my cslib#863 (general modal logic) I do a couple of similar things, namely PFunctor.const and PFunctor.unary. We should agree on terminology -- otherwise I see that the same things arose from two different contexts as a very promising sign. I think what I called unary is called monomial in cslib#863. I think that's basically where the overlap stops, so we're talking about something very small.

Also, I treated PFunctor.const as a def instead of an abbrev. Treating it as an abbrev was a pain for my modal logic development, since otherwise making a good grind pattern database is problematic (or at least it didn't work with the way I tried). Would having a def break something useful to you?
Also a good reminder that I've been sitting on a name change from X to y with that PR to match recent PolyFun changes as well

I don't think having a def is a problem off the top of my head. Maybe depends on the reducibility though, like can you still pass a raw value as a P.A value or do we need constructors for shapes if we fully hide the internals

I guess that also relates to the fact that PolyFun tends to choose more specific canonical presentations than is strictly necessary, rather than something like your Unary class which is maybe more generic

good question, I don't know: what I define as const, now that I look more carefully, is the constant child map, not the constant PFunctor. I typically define PFunctor constructors as abbrevs like you do.

See here: https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/863/changes#diff-01853467f9a503bcc329eab7ca1d45f0ecf317b73951b1c06e3c368cbda09a85

Devon Tuma said:

I guess that also relates to the fact that PolyFun tends to choose more specific canonical presentations than is strictly necessary, rather than something like your Unary class which is maybe more generic

Ah, yes. I have classes like Unary, and then in concrete developments I use canonical reps, like mkUnary for Hennessy-Milner Logic.

i don't know if it's relevant in your development(s), but in modal logic it allowed me to formulate lots of results that hold across entire families of logics, which is very nice. For example, here I prove lots of results that hold for all modal logics with a unary pfunctor signature: https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/863/changes#diff-23c39ac3c38315fedf926e8e960776e624aab40fef61da484d08aa2ea256c2f0
Btw, if there's a better name for my PFunctor.const, I'm happy to rename to avoid conflicts. I called it const inspired by Function.const, really. Suggestions welcome.
@Thomas Waring if you could have a look to judge whether the logical part of cslib#863 makes sense, we can deal with these issues separately.
I was going to suggest renaming mine to PFunctor.C to match polynomial stuff...
I think the abbrev is motivated by semireducible types being unpleasant in lean

Devon Tuma said:

I was going to suggest renaming mine to PFunctor.C to match polynomial stuff...

Oh, that sounds pretty good actually.
Maybe there's something to learn from how category theory handles the same problem
I think we've converged on abbrev, the overlap was only apparent. My const is really a different definition, and I'm pretty convinced it should be a def.

This has made me read some pieces of PolyFun, exciting to see the reuse of our semantics APIs! :-)

(I think we have lots to gain from building a solid PFunctor infrastructure in CSLib.)

Fabrizio Montesi said:

i don't know if it's relevant in your development(s), but in modal logic it allowed me to formulate lots of results that hold across entire families of logics, which is very nice. For example, here I prove lots of results that hold for all modal logics with a unary pfunctor signature: https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/863/changes#diff-23c39ac3c38315fedf926e8e960776e624aab40fef61da484d08aa2ea256c2f0

I think also there is probably useful stuff for us here, right now we basically encourage people to "pre-canonicalize" definitions but I think there is some nicer way to handle this along these lines. 0 * P or 0 ⊗ P satisfying the same class as 0 maybe seems like the obvious example of this being convenient (currently the library would suggest mapping explicitly through an additional equivalence because we lack those classes)
Do you think it would make sense for this PR to actually reverse the direction of the normalization? I know that some other monads take that direction
This I think is the opposite of a PR I created a while ago

Fundamentally the friction here is that Bind.bind isn't universe polymorphic, and so we either have to opt out of polymorphism, opt out of lean's builtin monad machinery, or have two copies of everything.
I see, I had just remembered this same problem getting resolved the other way for PMF awhile back
It would be nice if there could at least be a tag like to_additive
Not sure if that's possible when the universe generic version isn't also typeclass based
Perhaps there is a Lean RFC to be made here to at least allow the notation classes to be polymorphic, even if do and Monad will never be
Though last time I tried a trivial upstream universe generalization it wasn't received well, and this one is likely to be slightly less trivial...

I'm confused by things like

@[simp] lemma mul_def (P : PFunctor.{uA₁, uB₁}) (Q : PFunctor.{uA₂, uB₂}) :
    P * Q = P.prod Q := rfl

in cslib#803. We usually do the opposite for both simp and grind: shouldn't notation be the normal form?
Also, I'm not too familiar with the literature, is the notation y^ standard there perhaps?
The y^ notation was drawn from https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00990 originally (they call it that after Yoneda lemma I think)
The add/mul normalization direction I'm happy to change. Eric had suggested just only defining the notation which avoids this completely but the add notation is slightly worse type for type inference
Again for universe level reasons

Thanks, that's been a very useful read!

I find the fact that y is used in three different notations for three different things very confusing, though the algebra seems to yield isomorphic things when the different ys are applied to what's expected.
I think we could reasonably just say only monomial A B should be in core cslib, A y^ B isn't even especially shorter
Especially when e.g. 0 y^ 0 = 0 or 1 y^ 0 + 0 = 1 only hold up to isomorphism for PFunctor

Devon Tuma said:

The add/mul normalization direction I'm happy to change. Eric had suggested just only defining the notation which avoids this completely but the add notation is slightly worse type for type inference

I wonder if it's possible to define a high-priority override for + and *, which throws unsupportedSyntax if the arguments are not PFunctors and falls back to the usual + and *
Given that everything is only up to isomorphism and so = is meaningless, perhaps it makes sense to skip the notation entirely?
I had also considered using append notation to signal the fact that the order of interfaces is important
